target_customer: Businesses, brands and nonprofits buying event, portrait, product and real estate photography and video
problem: Companies needing professional photos or video had to find, vet and coordinate photographers themselves; Pretty Instant handled booking, staffing, editing and delivery.
business_model: Marketplace of vetted 1099 photographers with a service margin, plus roaming photo booth event revenue

founders.name: Ben Maitland-Lewis
previous_startups: Digital asset management platform for creative enterprise, sold to UMG (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Professional musician and tour manager before SonyBMG, per YC page.

founders.name: Chris Cave
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC page; no bio.

founders.name: Douglas E. Rogers
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page as technical co-founder.

founders.name: Chase McAleese
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC page; no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking marketplace and photo booth workflow with delivery tooling; operational complexity exceeded technical complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Photographer supply and booking are widely available through many marketplaces and local vendors; little lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A fellow YC photography marketplace, Snappr, acquired Pretty Instant in August 2021 and moved customer photos to its platform.

market_need_then: Event and corporate photography demand was served by fragmented local vendors; evidence of demand is limited to the company's later claim of serving about 3,500 brands (sources disagree between 2,000 and 3,500).

branding.domain_note: Used prettyinstant.com, which now redirects to the Snappr acquisition post.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful, tied to the instant photo booth idea

branding.brand_signature: Roaming photo booth that sends branded photos instantly

brand_strength.rationale: Name fit the photo booth origin but no press about the brand itself was found, and it was folded into Snappr.

pivots.to: Marketplace for professional photography and videography
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; inferred from the company descriptions, which list the photo booth as a later add-on.

outcome_analysis: Pretty Instant grew from a roaming photo booth into a professional photography marketplace and reportedly served thousands of brands, but no funding beyond YC was verified and the business was sold to its peer Snappr in August 2021 for an undisclosed price. The record does not support a clear cause for the sale.
notes: Website redirects to a Medium post about the Snappr acquisition; that post returned 403 so it was not read. Funding in aggregators (Bounce Watch 120K in 2015 and 1.3M in 2017, Gust) is unverified and not recorded as rounds. Founding year conflicts: a 2014 city planning agency profile says launched in 2011 by Marty Nee, descriptions say active 2012 to 2020, YC says W15. Competitor search found no dated competitor sources near the batch, so the list is empty. Founder titles vary across sources. The Snappr press release page only returned navigation text.
